result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` so their code now matches the docstrings. After the fixes I tested all 150 rules against a reference calculation built from each docstring (quantities 0–299, 8 unit prices), and none of them differ.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02 | Used `round` instead of rounding down to the won | Changed to `// 100` (floor) |
| 14 | Started at 101+ units | Now starts at 100+ |
| 72 | Started at 51+ units | Now starts at 50+ |
| 102, 109 | Started at 6+ units | Now start at 5+ |
| 57 | Started at 31+ units | Now starts at 30+ |
| 94 | Used `> 30` | Changed to `>= 30` |
| 79 | Gave 4% off | Changed to 3% |
| 58, 84, 116 | Capped the price instead of the discount (`min(base, cap)`) | Now caps the discount |
| 128 | Marginal rule computed the discount on the full order | Now discounts only units above 10 |

Rules 57 and 94 never charged a wrong price, because a marginal discount is 0 at the threshold anyway. I changed them only so the code reads like the docstring.

STATUS: DONE
